T01.reasoning: Hatched variant of the funnel sign T40; rarely after numbers and mostly inside sign groups with T18/T28/T16, as name or title elements are.

T02.reasoning: A filled bulb with a spike, mostly at the end of a line after other signs and sometimes after numbers. It could be a product qualifier; the food reading is weak.

T03.reasoning: A grid with long prongs, like a comb or heddle. It rarely follows numbers and pairs with the star sign T18, so it may be an institution or name element instead.

T04.reasoning: A round sign with horizontal lines that almost always follows a number and clusters with T25 and T38 in the same lists. It looks like one of a set of graded animal categories (circle-based sheep signs).

T05.reasoning: Very frequent. It usually stands next to the high-title sign T35 and seldom directly after a number, which suggests a title or profession.

T06.reasoning: A circle with a cross; it follows numbers in 14 of 17 lines, is very widespread and pairs with other circle-based animal signs (T23, T21).

T07.reasoning: A crosshatched pointed body with small side triangles. It follows numbers sometimes; the vessel reading is a guess from the shape (cross-hatching could also mean cloth).

T08.reasoning: A head profile with a ladder inside. It usually follows numbers and co-occurs with T35, so it may be a category of counted workers.

T09.reasoning: A simple cross. It appears after T06 (sheep) as in '#8 T06 T09' and after numbers, so it may be a goat or kid. MAŠ is also used for 'half' and in titles.

T10.reasoning: A head-profile sign with an outer hatched arc. It appears with T35 and T36 in name or title strings.

T11.reasoning: A building-like box with a grid and foot. It is very frequent, usually in sign groups and line-final, and not counted, which fits an institution or building.

T12.reasoning: A curved ladder shape that follows numbers in some lines ('#8 T12') and sits in compounds in others. The reading of the object is uncertain.

T13.reasoning: A branching plant drawing that pairs strongly with T15. It is sometimes counted, which fits a plant product or tree.

T14.gloss: agent / profession (hand or foot with object)
T14.reasoning: It never follows a number and is often line-final in sign groups, so it is a qualifier rather than a commodity. It looks like a hand or foot holding something.

T15.reasoning: A D-shape with strokes that follows numbers often (14/23) and pairs with the plant sign T13. It could be a container or measure of a plant product.

T16.reasoning: A stem with crossbars or chevrons, often line-final after numbers ('#4 T16'), so it is a counted item. It looks like a plant or reed, perhaps a feathered item.

T17.reasoning: A plain head profile. It sits in name and title groups with T18 and T03, which fits head-count or person use.

T18.reasoning: An eight-pointed star; the second most frequent target. It almost always appears inside sign groups, not after numbers, as a deity name or divine determinative does in temple-office names.

T19.reasoning: Two horizontal strokes crossed by a slanting stroke. It rarely follows a number and sits mid-group with T06 and T35. The reading is weak.

T20.reasoning: A rectangle with an inner bar. It mostly sits in sign groups with T35 and T24 rather than after numbers.

T21.reasoning: A pointed boat-like shape that mostly follows numbers and co-occurs heavily with T06 (sheep), so it is probably another animal category.

T22.reasoning: Clearly a fish drawing (body, ribs, tail). It almost always follows numbers, so it is a counted commodity.

T23.reasoning: The sheep circle-cross with added wedges. It follows numbers and co-occurs with T06, so it is a sheep subtype (male or young).

T24.reasoning: Very frequent. It combines with T40 in 68 of its lines, which looks like a fixed title compound. It is sometimes counted ('#1 T24'), perhaps as a person.

T25.reasoning: A circle with two lines, a sister of T04. It follows numbers in 20 of 28 lines and clusters with T04 and T38, which looks like graded herd categories.

T26.reasoning: An arrow drawing. It is often counted ('#4 T26') but also appears in names. A counted object is the weak guess.

T27.reasoning: A head inside a circle with a projection. Rare, often after numbers, paired with T12 and T32, so it may be a class of counted persons.

T28.reasoning: A lens shape with lines. It is never counted and often pairs with T09 and T12 in names. The object reading is uncertain.

T29.reasoning: A head with hatching at the mouth. It follows numbers in 11 of 15 lines and pairs with the household sign T11, which fits a ration or food allocation sign.

T30.reasoning: A head-like pointed sign with a small appendage that sits in groups with T35, T14 and T12. A person category is a guess.

T31.reasoning: A figure with a round head and a long horizontal shaft, perhaps a plough or a bent person. It is usually line-final after other signs, as titles are.

T32.reasoning: A head with a grid at the back. Rare; it pairs with T15, T35 and T27 and is sometimes after numbers.

T33.reasoning: A gridded rectangle, very frequent, mostly inside sign groups with T35, and not counted. It fits a field or a building or institution.

T34.reasoning: A stick figure with legs and an arm. It co-occurs with T18 and T35 in name and title groups.

T35.reasoning: By far the most frequent sign. It is seldom directly counted and heads many title and name compounds, as a top office title would.

T36.reasoning: A hand- or foot-like shape related to T14, inside sign groups. A profession or action qualifier is a weak guess.

T37.reasoning: A plain rectangle that co-occurs with T35, T24 and T25. The reading is very uncertain.

T38.reasoning: A crossing-strokes sign that follows numbers in 15 of 22 lines and pairs heavily with T25 and T04, so it may belong to the same herd-category set.

T39.reasoning: Rare; it pairs with T35, T40 and T12 and is sometimes counted. The object is unclear.

T40.reasoning: A funnel shape that almost always follows T24 (68 lines), which suggests a fixed title such as 'chief of X'. It is sometimes counted with '#1'.

_script_recognised: Yes, very likely Uruk-period proto-cuneiform from Mesopotamia (late 4th millennium BC), going by the sign shapes (star, circle-cross sheep, fish, EN-like sign) and the setting. Only a few signs (AN, EN, UDU, KU6, MAŠ, tentatively SAG and TI) are flagged as recognised from memory. The rest are inferred.
